title: CouncilProtocolV1
description: Frozen, typed, cross-repo execution contract between gitmoot (core; sole issuer of every record kind except council_result) and council (bash/python seats; producer of council_result only, consumer of everything else). One JSON document = one immutable record. Nothing here is ever updated in place: the 'current state' of any entity (a lease, an advancement decision, a CI observation) is always a fold over the most-recent record sharing that entity's correlation key, computed by the reading consumer, never a mutated row. record_type is the sole discriminator; every record kind repeats the same five envelope properties (protocol_version, record_id, record_type, issued_by, issued_at) directly in its own flat properties/required list rather than via allOf/unevaluatedProperties inheritance, to avoid the additionalProperties-with-allOf failure class one of the three source drafts caught in its own self-review. No field whose value is prose (summary, message, notes) may be parsed by any consumer to drive control flow (audit coding rule 5) -- every decision-bearing fact has a typed, enum- or digest-constrained sibling field. Identifiers in this protocol (record_id, task_id, attempt_id, root_id, ...) are NEWLY MINTED opaque tokens issued by gitmoot-core at record-persist time; they are deliberately NOT gitmoot's internal hierarchical jobs.id (which is slash-delimited, e.g. 'parent/delegation/<id>/retry/<n>', and used directly as a filesystem worktree path segment -- see FIXTURES-PLAN.md). Correlating a protocol identifier back to the internal jobs.id/tasks.id it was minted for is a new database column gitmoot must add (P0-1), not a re-typing of the existing column. See DESIGN.md for full rationale, CRB/R foreclosure citations, the audit-§9 coverage matrix, and the decision log recording which of the three source drafts (or which synthesis) won each contested point and why.

ProtocolVersion.description: Frozen protocol version. Any field change that is not purely additive (new optional property, new enum member with a documented default handling) ships as 2.0.0 with a dual-parse deprecation window; see DESIGN.md decision log #1.

Id.description: Opaque, gitmoot-core-minted identifier (ULID recommended). Equality-only; never parsed for structure or meaning by any consumer. Deliberately excludes '/' and ':' -- unlike gitmoot's internal jobs.id, which is slash-delimited and reused as a worktree path segment. Protocol identifiers (record_id, task_id, attempt_id, root_id, delegation_id, lease_id, ...) are NEW values minted at record-persist time and correlated back to gitmoot's internal row via a new DB column, never derived by parsing or truncating jobs.id (see FIXTURES-PLAN.md and DESIGN.md decision log #2).

Timestamp.description: RFC3339 UTC, always core-stamped (server clock). Never accepted verbatim from a caller or model (coding rule 5).

GitSha.description: Full git object id, lowercase hex: exactly 40 characters (SHA-1) or exactly 64 (SHA-256 git repositories). Abbreviated SHAs are never protocol-legal -- an abbreviated prefix is not a unique object id, which reopens exactly the ambiguity CRB-15/CRB-09 exist to close. GitHub API responses (the real data source) are always full-length, so there is no operational reason to admit a shorter pattern.

BranchName.description: Valid git ref name. Deliberately permits '/' (CRB-15: a narrow branch-name regex must not reject legitimate defaults such as release/next) while excluding whitespace, control characters, '..', a leading/trailing/doubled '/', and a trailing '.lock'.

hex.description: Lowercase sha256 hex digest of the exact byte content addressed (file, config, canonicalized JSON, diff, ...), computed by the core or a trusted backend from bytes it read itself -- never accepted as a caller-supplied unkeyed hash (coding rule 6).

ContentDigest.description: Locked to sha256 only for v1 (no multi-algorithm branch) -- decisive, matches existing codebase precedent (content_sha256 fields), and avoids inventing an algorithm-negotiation surface no implementation needs yet (coding rule 2).

resolved_path.description: Informational only -- the pathname observed when the digest was computed. NEVER re-read by pathname later; identity is `digest`, not this string (forecloses CRB-01, CRB-10, R-20's mutable-path-as-identity pattern).

CredentialRef.description: Opaque reference into a credential store, resolved server-side by gitmoot-core at spawn time. Never the raw secret, never an env var name, never a filesystem path or symlink target (forecloses R-12/R-13's credential-symlink and ambient-passthrough defects). This is net-new infrastructure -- see FIXTURES-PLAN.md / DESIGN.md decision log #9 for the interim compatibility shape needed alongside today's ambient env-var credential passthrough.

RuntimeFamily.description: Exactly gitmoot's registered runtime adapter set (internal/runtime/adapter.go: CodexRuntime, ClaudeRuntime, KimiRuntime, KimiCLIRuntime, ShellRuntime -- confirmed exhaustive by registry_test.go). No invented members (no 'glm', no 'gemini' -- those are Council-side bridge profiles that run THROUGH the 'claude' or 'codex' adapter against a non-default API endpoint, see BridgeProfile, not distinct gitmoot runtimes; coding rule 2/R-14: do not model an interface production does not implement).

EphemeralRuntimeFamily.description: Subset of RuntimeFamily legal for an ephemeral (unregistered, on-demand) worker -- matches gitmoot's EphemeralRuntimes exactly (internal/workflow/result.go). 'kimi-cli' and 'shell' are never legal ephemeral targets.

ExecutionMode.description: R-12's required 'explicit backend capability contract, no hidden tools in text-only mode.' Whether this attempt's backend may invoke tools/shell/filesystem access beyond producing text. A bridge/text-only reviewer (e.g. council-zai-glm) MUST be execution_mode=text_only; the runtime adapter is required to enforce this at spawn (sandboxed/no-tool invocation), not merely declare it here.

AutonomyPolicy.description: Ordinal write-authority: read_only(0) < workspace_write(1) < danger_full_access(2). 'auto' is deliberately NOT protocol-legal (R-10: 'auto' resolving differently per host/runtime is exactly the ambient-authority pattern coding rule 5 forbids -- confirmed live in internal/cli/agent_permissions.go's readOnlyImplementationBlocked comment: 'auto emits no --permission-mode ... non-deterministic across hosts'). CLI ergonomics may still accept 'auto' from an operator; gitmoot-core must resolve it to one concrete member of this enum before any record here is issued.

DelegationAction.description: Matches ResultDecisions-adjacent DelegationFailurePolicies/action set exactly as validated by internal/workflow/result.go's validateAgentResult (action must be one of ask, review, implement).

DecisionValue.description: Byte-identical to gitmoot's existing ResultDecisions (internal/workflow/result.go) -- unchanged so the decision vocabulary itself is not a migration break.

root_id.description: The top-level council run this attempt descends from. Equals task_id for a root attempt.

task_id.description: Stable across repair/retry rounds of one logical unit of work. Newly minted per dispatched unit (every ask/review/implement leg gets one, not only implement legs -- needed so review allocation (CRB-09/CRB-14) and repair binding (CRB-08) have their own lineage key independent of the writer's). NOT gitmoot's internal branch-scoped Task.ID: when an implement attempt's task_id has a corresponding gitmoot Task row, they may share a value by construction, but a task_id is required even for ask/review dispatches that never create a Task row.

parent_attempt_id.description: The delegating attempt's attempt_id, or null for a root attempt.

attempt_id.description: Unique per (re)execution. A retried/repaired task mints a new attempt_id while task_id stays stable. This is the fencing/correlation unit every other record binds to -- not job_id reuse.

attempt_ordinal.description: 1-based sequence of this attempt within task_id (1st implement = 1, repair-1 = 2, repair-2 = 3, ...).

delegation_id.description: The parent's council_result.delegations[].id that produced this attempt, or null for a root attempt.

delegation_depth.description: 0 for a root attempt; parent depth + 1 otherwise. Checked against the parent's DelegationGrant.max_depth.

PullRequestRef.description: number/url are both null iff state=none, both present otherwise -- schema-enforced (not merely documented, resolving an open question two of the three source drafts left to the binding generator).

provider_repo_id.description: The provider's own immutable opaque repository id (e.g. GitHub's numeric/node repository id), NOT owner/name text. For provider=local (no remote, dev/test flows): digest(first_commit_sha + normalized-absolute-init-path), itself then treated as an opaque string and never reopened by that path (resolves an open question two of the three source drafts left unresolved).

canonical_repo_key.description: digest(provider + provider_repo_id). The sole key for daemon service labels, locks, and cross-record repo identity (forecloses CRB-01: distinct repositories mapping to the same launchd/systemd label via sanitized owner/repo text).

full_name.description: owner/name. Advisory/display only -- rename/transfer-safe consumers key on canonical_repo_key, never on this string.

default_branch.description: Accepts any valid provider branch name including names containing '/' (forecloses CRB-15's narrow-regex default-branch defect).

base_sha.description: Exact default-branch SHA resolved and persisted at allocation time (CRB-15).

required_base_sha.description: Optional dependency-ordering ancestry requirement. When set, base_sha MUST be a descendant of this SHA, checked atomically (fetch remote default branch, resolve SHA, compare-and-swap) at allocation; allocation fails before any task/worktree/job is created if not (forecloses CRB-15).

head_sha.description: Exact immutable pushed head. null only pre-push (planning records); every review/verdict/gate record requires it non-null.

review_round.description: Monotonic ordinal scoped to (repository, pr.number), assigned transactionally under the same allocation lock CRB-09 requires for worktree creation -- NOT a value the wire type alone makes race-free (see DESIGN.md decision log #7 and FIXTURES-PLAN.md for the required one-time backfill of gitmoot's existing string-typed review_round values, e.g. 'review-1' or a bare job.ID fallback, into this integer form). A VerdictRecord is pinned to an exact (head_sha, review_round) pair; a stale pair can never gate a newer head (forecloses CRB-09, CRB-14).

roster_id.description: Resolved from the selected roster mode to a stable id -- never re-read as an env var at execution time (forecloses CRB-02).

roster_digest.description: Digest of the fully-resolved roster definition at contract-persist time.

seat_digest.description: Digest of the seat's resolved command/script content, not a wrapper pathname (forecloses CRB-10: stale wrapper paths remaining dispatchable after re-adoption).

kit_revision.description: Council kit checkout commit the seat script was read from.

kit_digest.description: Digest of the full kit tree consumed (templates, OMP yaml, lib/), not just the one seat file.

profile_id.description: e.g. 'zai-glm', 'devin-kimi'. A Council-side profile that routes a registered RuntimeFamily adapter (today always 'claude' or 'codex') against a non-default API endpoint/backend model.

endpoint_digest.description: Digest of the resolved, non-default API base-URL/endpoint configuration actually bound for this attempt (e.g. ZAI_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL). Makes an endpoint swap after validation structurally visible (R-12), the same way config_digest does for OMP config.

BridgeProfile.description: R-12's typed backend-capability contract for Council's real production bridge seats (council-zai-glm routes CLAUDE_BIN=claude against api.z.ai; council-devin-kimi is the analogous Devin-backed bridge). null on RuntimeIdentity.bridge_profile for a direct-provider attempt.

model.description: Runtime-scoped model identifier as actually invoked. A free string bounded by shape only -- deliberately not a closed enum; the runtime-scoped model catalog changes faster than the protocol should need to (validated against a registered-model catalog at the adapter layer, not in this schema).

executable_digest.description: Content digest of the actual runtime binary invoked for this attempt (never its pathname/inode alone).

config_digest.description: Digest of the fully-resolved OMP/roster/profile config content actually loaded, so a config pathname edited post-enqueue cannot affect an in-flight attempt (CRB-02).

dependency_digests.description: Full interpreter/tool/shared-library/dependency closure (R-20): a copied script whose shebang still resolves ambient /usr/bin/env is not represented as hermetic here.

advisor_enabled.description: Advisor process was initialized for this attempt.

advisor_required.description: Single canonical required-intervention flag, collapsing the two divergent knobs COUNCIL_OMP_ADVISOR_REQUIRED / COUNCIL_OMP_REQUIRE_ADVISOR (CRB-04).

backend_supports_split_thinking.description: Whether the OMP backend can express independent doer/advisor reasoning levels. False for today's OMP (one global thinking flag).

then.description: When the backend cannot split effort, doer/advisor thinking fields must be structurally ABSENT (not merely equal) -- there is nowhere in the document for two different levels to be written at all, so CRB-04's exact contradiction ('COUNCIL_OMP_THINKING=high' vs OMP YAML 'medium') is unrepresentable rather than merely undetected.

allOf.description: Intervention cannot be required from an advisor that was never initialized.

advisor_intervened.description: True only on a backend-produced typed receipt of an actual intervention -- never derived from counting a marker string in untrusted log output (forecloses CRB-05's `grep -c ... || echo 0` -> "0\n0" defect: there is no free-text count field anywhere in this schema for that bug class to live in).

host_id.description: Stable machine identity, not hostname alone (hostnames collide/change).

process_start_identity.description: Platform-native unforgeable start-time token: Linux /proc/<pid>/stat starttime (jiffies since boot) + boot id, or Darwin KERN_PROC start-time + session/pgid. Opaque to this schema; used to detect a PID recycled by an unrelated process after the real writer exited (CRB-12: 'children may fork, reparent, or survive SIGKILL of the launcher').

attempt_id.description: The attempt this grant is the ceiling FOR (the child, or the root if issuer_attempt_id is null).

issuer_attempt_id.description: The delegating parent attempt whose own grant this was carved from, or null for a root attempt's grant (issued directly from operator/profile policy).

repo_scope.description: digest of the canonical_repo_key set this grant may act within.

branch_scope.description: Empty = no branch may be written; non-empty = exact allowed branch name(s)/prefix(es).

unrestricted_delegatable.description: Whether this holder may grant danger_full_access to a child. Default false for every ask/review-only agent.

max_width.description: Max sibling delegations at one level.

budget_snapshot.description: Cumulative spend against root_id's delegation tree BEFORE this grant, folded by the core over every prior DelegationGrant sharing root_id at issuance time. Answers the audit's uncovered 14th concern (a ceiling alone does not stop repeated re-requesting from exceeding a tree-wide budget) without a separate ledger record kind -- the running total is always re-derivable from existing DelegationGrant rows.

grant_digest.description: digest of this grant's canonicalized content. A child's grant is verified server-side to be a field-for-field subset of the parent's grant (by attempt_id lookup, not by a caller-echoed digest) at BOTH result-advancement time and immediately before daemon materialization (CRB-16's two-checkpoint requirement) -- this subset check is a cross-record engine invariant, not expressible as a single-instance JSON Schema constraint; see DESIGN.md decision log #4.

allOf.description: A denied grant cannot smuggle a non-empty action or target set (CRB-16 negative path: an ask-only agent reaching dispatchDelegations at all becomes syntactically impossible).
danger_full_access is structurally excluded from the holder's own delegatable ceiling unless explicitly unlocked.

DelegationGrant.description: FIELD GROUP 8. Core-issued, immutable, 1:1 with attempt_id. Every child a holder delegates must be a subset of both this grant and operator/profile policy (validated server-side, see grant_digest description and DESIGN.md decision log #4, which also records why this synthesis DROPS the two source drafts' seat-held signature/attestation mechanisms as unnecessary net-new cryptographic infrastructure).

lease_id.description: Stable across a lease's own acquire/renew/release/expire/reclaim transitions; each transition is a NEW WriterLease record sharing this lease_id (append-only -- there is no in-place update).

worktree_id.description: Never a raw filesystem path -- a worktree path is mutable/reassignable; its id is not.

fencing_token.description: Strictly increasing per (task_id, worktree_id); never reused, never decreases across recovery, and doubles as this record's append-only order key within that scope. Any component asked to accept a write (git push, DB commit, provider mutation) MUST reject a fencing_token lower than the highest it has already observed for that (task_id, worktree_id) -- the standard fencing-token pattern, which is what makes CRB-12's orphaned writer harmless even if it eventually wakes up and tries to finalize.

reclaimed_from_lease_id.description: The prior lease_id this record supersedes. Required non-null when state=reclaimed so an orphan-recovery event always has full lineage (CRB-12 acceptance: 'exactly one deterministic recovery outcome is recorded').

deadline.description: FIELD GROUP 9. caller_deadline_seconds (e.g. an interactive council-run's patience) and backend_timeout_seconds (e.g. the OMP seat's independent `timeout --foreground`) are separate fields on purpose so CRB-12's exact observed mismatch (3600s vs 5400s, disagreeing, discovered live) is visible in the contract before launch. The core MUST reject a lease where backend_timeout_seconds > caller_deadline_seconds before enqueue; JSON Schema 2020-12 has no `$data` keyword to express that cross-field inequality natively, so it is enforced by the generated consumer, not this schema alone (documented, not a silent gap -- see DESIGN.md decision log #5).

WriterLease.description: FIELD GROUP 9/10 (deadline + writer/supervisor lease fencing). Exactly one exclusive writer lease per (task_id, worktree_id) at a time; a second writer must be rejected until the highest fencing_token record for that scope shows state in {released, expired-and-reclaimed}. Reviews never hold or require a WriterLease (they key off head_sha alone -- see GitRefState/VerdictRecord), so CRB-09's race is never contended by a reviewer, only by a genuine second writer.

EphemeralSpec.description: Matches internal/prompts/contract_generated.go's delegationSchemaHelp EphemeralSpec fields exactly. All requested_* fields are HINTS ONLY -- never authoritative. The materialized child's effective identity is whatever its own ExecutionContract says, resolved by gitmoot-core against the issuing DelegationGrant's ceiling, never against these hints directly.

content_digest.description: Digest of the post-change content (pre-change for delete) -- not diff text, so it survives whitespace-insensitive re-hashing.

diff_artifact_id.description: artifact_id of a stored unified-diff ArtifactRef.

argv.description: Exact argv, not a shell string. A pipelined/composed command is represented as one sh -c "..." argv[0]/argv[1] pair by the producing wrapper -- this schema does not add a separate shell:bool escape hatch (kept simple; see DESIGN.md decision log #6).

TypedCommand.description: Replaces free-text 'tests_run: ["go test ./..."]' strings. A claimed test is this record with exit_status==0; a non-zero exit_status here cannot be overridden by summary prose (CRB-06 acceptance #2). This exact instrumentation does not exist in any current seat script and is new engineering, not incidental to the schema -- see FIXTURES-PLAN.md.

evidence_artifact_id.description: changes_requested MUST carry >=1 TypedFinding with a bound artifact (forecloses CRB-06's evidence-free changes_requested).

id.description: Unique within this batch; deps[] reference it.

worktree.description: Requested worktree path HINT only; the child's actual worktree grant lives in its own DelegationGrant.worktree_scope, resolved server-side.

prompt.description: What the agent should do. Required -- matches gitmoot's real, currently-enforced validateAgentResult rule ('prompt is required') exactly. Dropping this field (as two of the three source drafts did) is a functional regression: a delegated child would receive no task description.

requested_model.description: Hint only, never authoritative -- see EphemeralSpec note.

TypedDelegation.description: Exactly one of agent or ephemeral must be set (enforced by the generated binding, matching gitmoot's existing Delegation.Agent/Ephemeral either/or shape). This record deliberately carries NO grant digest, signature, or attestation field from the untrusted seat -- see DelegationGrant description and DESIGN.md decision log #4 for why the two-checkpoint CRB-16 authority check is entirely server-side and needs no caller-presented credential on this record at all.

omp.description: Required non-null whenever the seat is OMP-backed; null for a plain ask/review/implement seat with no doer/advisor split.

persisted_at.description: Strictly before the job is enqueued (CRB-02: 'immutable execution contract persisted before enqueue').

contract_digest.description: digest computed over this record's canonicalized bytes AFTER persistence and stored alongside it (hash-then-store, not self-referential -- deliberately different from the rejected commit-contains-its-own-SHA design, §6.13). Every later record for this attempt_id (ExecutionRecord.matches_contract_digest, DelegationGrant) references this value.

ExecutionContract.description: FIELD GROUPS 1-7 assembled. The single immutable, pre-enqueue launch artifact. DelegationGrant, WriterLease, and every downstream execution/check/verdict/advancement/provider-effect record REFERENCE this contract by identity rather than being folded into it, so a downstream failure in any one of them can never mutate what was true at launch time (direct structural fix for CRB-13).

issued_by.description: The untrusted seat/agent name that produced this record (NOT 'gitmoot-core' -- this is the ONE record kind in the protocol that is model/seat-authored, and it is never treated as authoritative on its own: VerdictRecord is the core-validated projection that carries authority, ResultCheckRecord gates whether this record's evidence may even reach review/gate).

contract_digest.description: The ExecutionContract.contract_digest this attempt executed under -- lets the core detect a result reported against the wrong/stale contract.

summary.description: Human-readable only. MUST NOT be parsed by any control-flow path (coding rule 5) -- no grep/awk/regex over this field may ever gate branch, PR, repair, retry, gate, or continuation behavior. Its presence/non-emptiness is validated; its CONTENT is never authority. (The real, currently-shipping regression this guards against: kit/bin/council-continue-seat's existing regex scans exactly a summary-adjacent text blob for routing today -- a P0-3 static check should grep adapter source for this pattern; see FIXTURES-PLAN.md.)

allOf.description: CRB-06: decision=implemented with empty typed_changes/typed_commands is schema-invalid, not merely policy-warned.
Byte-identical to gitmoot's real, currently-enforced rule (validateAgentResult: 'decision skipped cannot be used with delegations').

CouncilResult.description: FIELD GROUPS 10 (partial) + evidence half of 11-12. THE ONLY record kind an untrusted model/seat authors. Typed replacement for the free-text gitmoot_result envelope in internal/prompts/contract_generated.go; council.sh's current unconditional empty-list emission (result["changes_made"]=[] etc. for every seat) is schema-illegal here whenever decision requires non-empty evidence. It is evidence, never a verdict: nothing reads council_result.decision as binding workflow authority by itself.

execution_state.description: Model/process execution truth ONLY, independent of verdict/result-check/advancement state (forecloses CRB-13).

observed_runtime.description: What actually ran, attested by the launch supervisor -- never self-reported by the model.

oneOf.description: Records the typed platform RAM probe actually used (sysctl hw.memsize on Darwin, /proc/meminfo on Linux), foreclosing CRB-11's silent zero-RAM collapse to a hardcoded minimum.

matches_contract_digest.description: Core-computed: true iff observed_runtime/observed_omp are field-for-field equal to the ExecutionContract's declared runtime/omp. False is a hard-fail condition upstream of any decision text (CRB-02 acceptance #5: 'reject any attempt whose effective identity does not match the persisted contract').

ExecutionRecord.description: FIELD GROUP 11a. Never claim a model/config/effort ran without this record (coding rule 17).

policy_mode.description: Explicit, per-attempt, core-enforced. 'block' means artifact preparation is impossible on failure (CRB-06 requirement); replaces today's silent Council-emits-empty-evidence vs Gitmoot-warns-only mismatch. Strict/'block' is the schema default policy_mode gitmoot-core assigns once a conformant CouncilResult producer exists (see FIXTURES-PLAN.md migration window).

ResultCheckRecord.description: FIELD GROUP 11b. Booleans are computed by gitmoot-core from the CouncilResult's typed_* arrays -- never from a word count over an untrusted log (CRB-05's bug class structurally excluded).

produced_by.description: The runtime identity that actually produced this vote -- an execution receipt, not a claimed roster entry (CRB-02).

decision_digest.description: Digest of the exact CouncilResult content this verdict was extracted from; tamper-evident and independently re-derivable.

head_sha.description: The exact head this verdict is bound to (CRB-14): a verdict does not silently re-bind when the writer produces a new head.

review_round.description: Paired with head_sha; a stale (head_sha, review_round) pair can never gate a newer head.

immutable.description: Once written, a verdict is never updated or deleted; it remains valid and usable even if a later AdvancementRecord for the same attempt fails (forecloses CRB-13's acceptance proof).

CiObservationRecord.description: Append-only raw observation, one row per merge-gate evaluation. Mirrors gitmoot's real, already-shipped merge_gate_ci_observations invariant (store.go #596: the gate must see a SECOND consecutive zero-external observation at the SAME head, at least min_ci_wait after the first, before concluding 'no CI' -- closing the race where a fresh head merges before a check run is created). This synthesis models the raw observations as append-only records; the two-consecutive-zero derivation is an engine-side fold over consecutive CiObservationRecord rows for one head_sha, stamped as GateIntentRecord.ci_state (added because none of the three source drafts modeled this already-shipped gitmoot invariant at all -- see critique-completeness.md finding 2.2).

verdict_record_ids.description: The exact set of VerdictRecord.record_id this gate evaluation is about to act on -- durably committed BEFORE gate execution.

gate_intent_digest.description: digest of this record's own canonicalized content. A gate process killed after persisting this record but before a verdict/advancement exists MUST replay against this exact digest on restart, never reconstruct intent from prompt/summary text (forecloses CRB-07's core failure: 'gate input/intent is not durably committed before gate execution').

GateIntentRecord.description: NEW record kind (absent from all three source drafts -- CRB-07's literal required change, 'persist a gate intent containing exact review receipts, CI observation, PR/head/base identity, and requested policy... before execution', was named by name in the audit but never modeled as its own record by any draft; see critique-completeness.md finding 2.1). AdvancementRecord.gate_intent_record_id references this.

sequence.description: Monotonic ordinal scoped to task_id. This record kind is append-only -- a new AdvancementRecord per evaluation, never an updated row; 'current' advance_state is the row with the highest sequence for a task_id. retry_count is len(records with advance_state=retryable) for this task_id, derivable by fold rather than stored redundantly.

triggering_record_id.description: The VerdictRecord.record_id or GateIntentRecord.record_id this evaluation consumed, or null for the first pending evaluation of a fresh gate_intent.

advance_state.description: Workflow fanout/continuation truth ONLY, independent of execution_state and verdict decision (CRB-13).

target_transition.description: Typed next-step, not a coordinator-reconstructed decision from prompt/summary text (forecloses CRB-07's repair-routing-via-summary-reconstruction defect).

AdvancementRecord.description: FIELD GROUP 11d. A gate process killed before any AdvancementRecord exists for a gate_intent_record_id MUST replay that identical gate_intent (see GateIntentRecord.gate_intent_digest); killed after one exists, it resumes from the highest-sequence record without rerunning valid votes (CRB-07 acceptance proof).

prior_attempt_id.description: The reviewed implement attempt this repair answers.

finding_ids.description: The specific TypedFinding.id values (from the VerdictRecord's underlying CouncilResult) this repair attempt is authorized to answer. A repair issued against a stale or wrong finding set is a structural mismatch a consumer can detect (forecloses CRB-08's gap: task/attempt ancestry alone proves 'another attempt of the same task', not 'this attempt answers findings F1..Fn').

expected_head_before.description: The head the new attempt's writer worktree MUST start from; a mismatch is rejected before the repair worktree materializes.

reused_branch.description: The existing implementation branch, reused in place (CRB-08: repair must reuse the existing task branch/worktree under an exclusive lease, never Council's current -vN new-branch versioning).

requested_by_attempt_id.description: The gate/coordinator attempt that authorized this repair.

RepairRequestRecord.description: NEW record kind (absent from all three source drafts -- CRB-08's literal required-change list: 'accepts immutable findings/receipt IDs; reuses the existing task branch and writer worktree under an exclusive lease; verifies exact PR/head/task ancestry; records head-before and expected head; preserves review/gate ancestry', restated as §9 Gate&Repair acceptance #4; see critique-completeness.md finding 2.3). A WriterLease for reused_worktree_id must be acquired under new_attempt_id before any repair commit is possible.

idempotency_key.description: Core-derived deterministic key over (effect_type, repository_key, target, requested_by_attempt_id, payload_digest). A crash-and-retry of the same intent is a provider-side no-op on replay, never a duplicate PR comment or a double merge.

requested_by_attempt_id.description: Issued by the trusted workflow only; candidate-controlled (tag-triggered) code never holds this authority (forecloses R-17).

ProviderEffectIntent.description: FIELD GROUP 13a. Written to the durable outbox BEFORE the mutating provider call is attempted (coding rule 11).

idempotency_key.description: Must equal the idempotency_key of exactly one ProviderEffectIntent.

observed_state.description: 'unknown' is the fail-closed outcome after an interruption where the provider's own state could not be re-confirmed (e.g. crash mid-merge). Reconciliation MUST resolve 'unknown' by re-querying the provider keyed on idempotency_key, never by re-attempting the mutation blind.

external_ref.description: Provider-native id of the effect (merge commit SHA, comment id, release asset id), or null if not applied.

migration_id.description: Stable id, not merely the ordinal integer gitmoot's current schema_migrations(version, applied_at) table uses (forecloses R-05: an ordinal-only ledger cannot detect content drift on an already-applied migration).

content_digest.description: digest of this migration's exact SQL/DDL content.

predecessor_digest.description: Chains to the prior migration's content_digest; a mismatch against a real predecessor fixture is refused (R-05, R-06).

storage_uri.description: Content-addressed store locator; the digest embedded in the URI MUST equal content_digest.hex (engine-enforced). Never a filesystem pathname -- an artifact can never be silently replaced at a stable path (coding rule 5).

ArtifactRef.description: FIELD GROUP 10. Every reference from CouncilResult/Finding/TypedCommand resolves to bytes through this record -- fixes a completeness gap where one of the three source drafts had no storage locator at all.
